title: Best Explainer Video Animators (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire an explainer video animator: what the package should include, how to brief the script, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: An explainer video shows in a minute or two what your product does and why it matters, which is hard to do in text. Most explainer projects run late or disappoint because the script changes after animation starts. This guide shows you how to lock the important decisions early.

faq.q: How long should an explainer video be?
faq.a: Shorter than you think. Most explainers cover one problem, one solution and one next step, and a short, clear video is usually watched to the end more often. Let the script decide the length, not the other way round.
Some animators include scriptwriting, others expect a finished script. If you write it, read it aloud and time it before ordering, because the length of the voice-over sets the length of the video.

faq.q: What animation style should I choose?
faq.a: Common styles are flat 2D characters, motion graphics with icons and text, whiteboard drawing, and 3D. Pick the one that suits your audience and budget, and look for that exact style in the animator's portfolio.
Often it is an extra. Ask whether a professional voice actor is included, which languages and accents are available, and whether you can approve the recording before animation.

faq.q: Can I make changes after the animation is done?
faq.a: Small changes usually fit within revisions. Changing the script or the style after animation has started often means redoing work, which costs time and money. Approve the script and storyboard carefully first.
